newsitem.title: Finland: Helsinki ends higher but confused as Lebed to go.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends higher but confused as Lebed to go.

text.p: Shares hit year-highs intra session and ended on stronger ground, but late reports that Russian security chief Alexander Lebed was sacked by president Boris Yeltsin left confusion, brokers said.
However, the underlying trend should be rising, they said.
"The trend is still good ... but there was the Lebed news, and we don't know if it's good or bad," said one.

Interim results from UPM-Kymmene and Metsa-Serla offered no positive surprises to those hoping for a fast recovery in forestries, but shares rose and stayed in positive territory as the January-August profits were partly better than expected.
The HEX ended at new year-high 2236.1, which was its highest level since September 1995. The previous year-high was 2226.6 set on October 8.
Unless Wall Street upsets investors, more gains were seen possible, particularly if Merita resumes its rally, but some brokers warned that bulls could soon hit a ceiling.
"This is pretty much a bull market ... it looks like it always does before it halts completely," said one broker. "Shares are vulnerable now if interest rates rise," he said.
